claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories with one package per repository, cohesive components grouped in a package, and multiple repositories for distinct packages.
Following the repository practices described improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages an organization builds and consumes.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), each versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply semver Git tag, run pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Private Registry publishing is a Pulumi Cloud / Pulumi IDP feature.
In both package types the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package, and a repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected; components ship together at the package's version.
The importance of the one-package-per-repository principles grows as an organization's Pulumi adoption grows.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Example layout: a PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root with components in a components/ directory defines a package.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed, which violates semver.
In the example, a package released at v1.0.0, then an enhancement to ComponentA yields v1.1.0, then a breaking change to ComponentB yields v2.0.0 (per semver minor/major bump rules).
